results.title: efficient lightweight railway track segmentation network for resource-constrained platforms with TensorRT | Intelligent Transportation Infrastructure | Oxford Academic
results.content: Considering this challenge, we propose an edge-enabled real-time railway track segmentation algorithm, which is optimized to be suitable for edge applications by optimizing the network structure and quantizing the model after training. In light of the above background, we propose a lightweight track segmentation algorithm founded on YOLOv8-seg and integrating advanced technologies such as pruning and quantization to implement an efficient and real-time track segmentation algorithm on edge devices. To the best of our knowledge, this approach is the first track segmentation algorithm in the railway domain that can achieve real-time performance on resource-constrained edge devices. Due to railway data security and privacy concerns, publicly available rail datasets are relatively rare, and the data quality is not high, which limits the training and generalization of deep learning models on railway track segmentation tasks. **Model acceleration and compression.** Model compression and acceleration are quite broad and active research areas in deep learning, aiming to speed up inference and reduce the computation, energy, and storage costs to adapt to resource-constrained environments such as embedded devices, mobile applications, and real-time systems. But to the best of our knowledge, the existing research on railway track segmentation tasks focuses on improving inference speed by designing lightweight network structures, and rarely considers collaborative optimization and acceleration on specific hardware platforms (e.g., GPU, CPU, FPGA). Latency refers to the time taken for the model to infer a single image, excluding the time required for pre- and post-processing, whereas the cost metric includes them. Compared with the baseline, the proposed method achieves mAP of 91.1% and 83.3% on detection and instance segmentation tasks, respectively, which are only reduced by 0.9% and 1.4%, while offering comparable or superior performance in terms of model complexity. **Analysis of the speedup effects on different devices.** As can be seen from Table 2 as well, the inference speed of our model (excluding pre- and post-processing time) using FP16 precision on the Jetson Nano is approximately 1.2 times that of FP32, whereas, on the GTX 3060Ti, it is 1.6 times faster. In this paper, we have proposed an efficient network algorithm designed for railway scenarios, capable of accomplishing real-time track segmentation on low-performance edge devices.

results.title: AI Learning in Resource-Constrained Environments - William Zujkowski
results.content: Train AI models on resource-constrained hardware with quantization, pruning, and distillation—run GPT-3 capabilities 100x faster through compression. Running large language models on a Raspberry Pi cluster taught me more about AI efficiency than years of unlimited cloud budgets. The conventional wisdom suggested that meaningful AI work required massive datasets, enormous models, and virtually unlimited compute resources. Single GPU training runs can cost $1,000-$10,000 for large models, and AWS/GCP credits run out fast (3-5 experiments can drain $500). RAM constraints (16-64GB typical) clash with models requiring 100GB+ for training. * Large "teacher" model (GPT-3 175B parameters) generates synthetic training data[1]. * Reduces training time by 10-100x compared to training large model from scratch. * Pre-trained efficient models available via Hugging Face: instant baseline for projects. * INT8 models run on specialized hardware: Tensor Cores, Neural Engine, dedicated AI accelerators. When I combined pruning and quantization on my BERT model, it ran 4x faster and used 75% less memory while maintaining 95% of original accuracy. * Zero training compute: use pre-trained model's general knowledge. * Training models to learn new tasks quickly with minimal examples. * Train ensemble of models with different initializations or architectures. Active learning reduced annotation requirements by 60% while maintaining model performance on my domain-specific classification task. * Domain confusion: train model to be unable to distinguish source vs. * Parameter efficiency: one model vs. * Quantization essential: INT8 models vs FP32 reduces memory 4x. My cluster of eight Raspberry Pi 4s now runs inference on models that previously required cloud GPUs. I tested this setup with BERT inference and found it handled 50-80 requests per second, which opened possibilities for edge AI deployment I hadn't considered before. * Memory usage: train large models on consumer GPUs (24GB vs 80GB A100). * Practical example: train 13B parameter model on 4x RTX 3090 vs requiring 8x A100. When I applied curriculum learning to my natural language understanding models in mid-2023, training time dropped by 30% while final accuracy improved. * Hardware portability: deploy same model on CPU, GPU, mobile, edge devices. * Large language models: can't train GPT-3 scale models on consumer hardware (requires 350GB+ VRAM). * Efficiency bootcamps: hands-on sessions optimizing real models on constrained hardware.

results.title: Neural Network Optimization for Resource-Constrained IoT Devices
results.content: (PDF) Neural Network Optimization for Resource-Constrained IoT Devices. Neural Network Optimization for Resource-Constrained IoT Devices. The rapid expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) has created an urgent need for neural networks that deliver reliable intelligence under stringent constraints of memory, compute, and energy. This paper presents a unified, deployment-oriented framework for neural network optimization on resource-constrained IoT devices, integrating structured pruning, post-training and quantization-aware quantization, knowledge distillation, and lightweight architectural redesign. We formalize a multi-objective cost function that balances accuracy, latency, model size, and energy per inference, and we operationalize it via a staged pipeline: (i) sparsity-inducing pruning with topology preservation for microcontroller kernels, (ii) mixed-precision quantization to 8- and 4-bit pathways with calibration on device-representative data, (iii) teacher-student distillation with temperature-scaled soft targets to recover accuracy, and (iv) hardware–software co-tuning for common IoT platforms (Raspberry Pi, ESP32, and Cortex-M microcontrollers). Neural Network Optimization for Resource-Constrained IoT. Neural Networks; IoT Devices; Optimization; Model Compression; Quantization; Pruning; Edge AI;. This manuscript delves into neural network optimization techniques designed for resource-constrained IoT. However, existing deep convolutional neural network models are computationally expensive and memory intensive, hindering their deployment in devices with low memory resources or in applications with strict latency requirements. To address these limitations, we describe a method to reduce the storage and computation required by neural networks by an order of magnitude without affecting their accuracy, by learning only the important connections. ### Neural Network Optimization for Resource-Constrained IoT Devices.
